events.title: Ponce de León Sights Florida
events.description: Spanish explorer Juan Ponce de León first sighted the coast of what is now Florida on or around this date during Easter season, and he later named the land La Florida.
events.significance: This marked the beginning of European exploration and colonization of Florida and the southeastern United States, a key step in Spain's expansion in the Americas.

events.title: Birth of Wilhelm Conrad Röntgen
events.description: Wilhelm Conrad Röntgen, the German physicist who discovered X-rays in 1895, was born in Lennep, Prussia.
events.significance: His discovery of X-rays revolutionized medicine and physics, and he received the first Nobel Prize in Physics in 1901.

events.title: First International Wireless Radio Transmission
events.description: Guglielmo Marconi sent a wireless signal across the English Channel from Wimereux, France, to South Foreland, England.
events.significance: The transmission showed that radio communication could span international distances, paving the way for transatlantic wireless telegraphy and modern telecommunications.

events.title: Great Alaska Earthquake
events.description: A magnitude 9.2 earthquake struck south-central Alaska near Prince William Sound on Good Friday, generating powerful tsunamis that caused destruction along the Pacific coast.
events.significance: It remains the most powerful earthquake recorded in North American history and the second most powerful worldwide, and it advanced the understanding of plate tectonics and tsunami warning systems.

events.title: Tenerife Airport Disaster
events.description: Two Boeing 747 jets, operated by KLM and Pan Am, collided on a fog-covered runway at Los Rodeos Airport in Tenerife, Canary Islands, killing 583 people.
events.significance: It is the deadliest accident in aviation history and led to major reforms in air traffic control communication, standard phraseology, and cockpit resource management.
